raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-M3.1-Flash NVIDIA support is in `main` ([#45925](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45925) and follow-ups), so the cookbook no longer needs the "install from the support PR (TBD)" step or the one-off `dev-minimax-m31-flash` image everywhere.

The latest release, v0.5.23, includes #45925. It does not include later fixes the recipes rely on, such as DSpark on Hopper (#46868), the DSpark draft KV TP placement fix (#46851) and the MSA plugin behind `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` (#46625). It also has no CUDA 13.4 image. So the page points at nightlies, not `latest`.

## Modifications

**Python install**
- Install SGLang from `main` instead of a PR checkout.
- Pin MSA to `1e7bf76f26a5f53cfc2d4d297e1ec2e40955e431`, the commit `docker/Dockerfile.cu134` pins.
- Run `git submodule update --init --recursive`, because MSA prefill compiles against its CUTLASS submodule.
- Install `integrations/sglang`, the MSA MonoKernel plugin that the Low-Latency recipe's `--monokernel-backend msa` loads. The previous pin `c8e1013` has no `integrations/` directory.
- Say that AMD support is not in `main` yet.

**Docker images** (`dockerImages` and the Docker tab)

| Hardware | Image | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GB300, GB200 | `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-cu134` | CUDA 13.4 nightly. It ships MSA and its plugin and is published for arm64 only. |
| H200 | `lmsysorg/sglang:dev` | cu130 nightly. Hopper does not use MSA or need CUDA 13.4. |
| B300, B200 | `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-minimax-m31-flash` (unchanged) | No x86_64 CUDA 13.4 nightly exists yet; #47999 adds one. |
| MI355X, MI350X | `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-minimax-m31-flash-mi35x` (unchanged) | The AMD integration ([#46693](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46693)) is still open. Also drops a trailing space from these two image strings. |

The AgentX snippets are dated benchmark records pinned by digest and are not touched.

## Testing

- Docs-only change.
- I checked on Docker Hub / registry that each image tag exists for the architecture listed above.
- I confirmed that `dev` (built from 38d9e4a3) contains #46868 and #46851.
- **Not run:** the recipes have not been re-run on `nightly-cu134` (GB300 / GB200) or on `dev` (H200).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).

 <Tab title="Python (pip / uv)">
 
-MiniMax-M3.1 support has not yet been merged into SGLang `main`. Install from the support PR below. The PR number is **TBD**; replace `TBD` with the actual PR number before running these commands.
+MiniMax-M3.1-Flash support on NVIDIA is in SGLang `main`. The latest release (v0.5.23) predates several fixes the recipes below rely on, so install from `main`. AMD MI350X / MI355X support is not in `main` yet; on AMD, use the Docker image.
 
 ```bash Command
 pip install --upgrade pip
 pip install uv
 
-PR_NUMBER=<the PR number of the model support PR>
 git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git
 cd sglang
-git fetch origin "pull/${PR_NUMBER}/head"
-git checkout FETCH_HEAD
 uv pip install --prerelease=allow -e python
 cd ..
 ```
 
-On NVIDIA Blackwell (B300 / GB300 / B200), also install the MSA sparse-attention kernels at the tested commit. SGLang imports them at startup, and the server fails without them. Hopper and AMD do not use them. Some of these kernels are compiled at runtime and need a **CUDA toolkit (`nvcc`) >= 13.4** on the machine. The CUDA version of the PyTorch wheel (`cu130`) does not count. See [Blackwell prerequisites](#blackwell-prerequisites).
+On NVIDIA Blackwell (B300 / GB300 / B200 / GB200), also install the MSA sparse-attention kernels at the commit the nightly CUDA 13.4 image pins. SGLang imports them at startup, and the server fails without them. The second install registers the MonoKernel plugin that the Low-Latency recipe's `--monokernel-backend msa` loads. Hopper and AMD do not use them. Some of these kernels are compiled at runtime and need a **CUDA toolkit (`nvcc`) >= 13.4** on the machine. The CUDA version of the PyTorch wheel (`cu130`) does not count. See [Blackwell prerequisites](#blackwell-prerequisites).
 
 ```bash Command
 git clone https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MSA.git
 cd MSA
-git checkout c8e1013a16a708d2a7656805d5fc26f2b87715d1
+git checkout 1e7bf76f26a5f53cfc2d4d297e1ec2e40955e431
+git submodule update --init --recursive
 uv pip install --no-deps -e .
+uv pip install --no-deps -e integrations/sglang
 cd ..
 ```

 ```bash Command
+docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-cu134

 docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:dev-minimax-m31-flash
+# NVIDIA H200 (nightly):
+docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:dev
 # AMD MI350X / MI355X (ROCm 7.2):
 docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:dev-minimax-m31-flash-mi35x
 ```
 
+The Blackwell images ship a CUDA 13.4 toolkit, which the MSA kernels need (see [Blackwell prerequisites](#blackwell-prerequisites)). The CUDA 13.4 nightly is published for arm64 only, so B300 and B200 stay on `dev-minimax-m31-flash` for now.
